title: Apple owes Taction $5.7B after losing haptic feedback IP trial
content:
An intellectual property lawsuit over the Apple Watch's Taptic Engine has resulted in a loss for Apple, as a jury ruled that it owes Taction more than $5.7 billion for infringing patents.


Apple's Taptic Engine - Image Credit: Apple
Apple and many other device manufacturers rely on haptic feedback to alert users that they have pressed a button successfully, as well as for alerts and message notifications. However, Apple's implementation of the concept has resulted in a very hefty legal bill.
In April 2021, Taction Technology sued Apple for allegedly infringing on a pair of Taction patents, which were supposedly used in the Taptic Engine. Over five years later, Reuters reports that a jury has sided against Apple on the matter.

title: Top Stories: Apple Leaks, Siri AI Settlement, and More
content:
The Apple rumor mill never stops, and this week MacRumors was able to break the news of details on several upcoming products.


We're also still learning more about the just-released iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max plus the upcoming iPhone Duo, while this week saw the debut of new Beats 360 headphones and the start of claim acceptance for the class action lawsuit over Siri AI delays, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more!

Top Stories

iPad Mini With A20 Pro, New HomePod Mini Colors, and New Apple TV 4K All Just Leaked

MacRumors this week leaked the next iPad mini, HomePod mini, and Apple TV 4K models, all of which are likely to be announced this October as part of another wave of product launches including an all-new operating system to accompany some of the new hardware.


The most notable iPad mini details revealed in the leaks include an A20 Pro chip, a new speaker design, and a landscape front camera, while images have revealed that the next HomePod mini will be available in new colors like green and pink. There is also evidence of an upcoming "Apple TV 4K (4th generation)" model, so it appears that a new Apple TV is finally coming soon after a four-year wait.

confirmed some rumored details for the 12th-generation iPad, although we're not expecting that to launch until early next year.

Siri AI Settlement Website Now Live: Apple to Pay Some iPhone Owners

In May, Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle a U.S. class action lawsuit over Siri AI's delayed launch, and the settlement website is now live.


Apple will pay an estimated $25 per eligible iPhone to eligible customers, who can submit a claim via the settlement website between September 21 and December 21 of this year. The exact payment may be higher or lower than $25 depending on the total number of valid claims submitted and other factors, with the maximum amount set at $95.

Apple denies all of the allegations made in the lawsuit, but agreed to the settlement to avoid the costs and risks of a trial.

iPhone 18 Pro Max Requires 'Prepare to Ship' Battery Drain Before Shipping

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has a single-cell battery capacity over 20 watt-hours, which means there are additional shipping requirements. If an ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max needs to be shipped somewhere, its maximum battery capacity has to be limited through firmware.


According to Apple, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max uses an "innovative battery-firmware solution" that limits battery capacity to below 20Wh between when the iPhone is manufactured and its delivery to a customer. Activating the iPhone removes the limit to make the battery's full charging capacity available.

Customers who need to ship the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max for repair, trade-in, or other purposes have to use a new Prepare to Ship feature. Prepare to Ship discharges the battery to below 20Wh and sets a charge limit so the iPhone stays below the threshold during the shipping process.

Apple Exec Says 'Hold Us Accountable' on iPhone Duo Crease

Apple hardware engineering VP Tom Marieb recently spoke with TechRadar and shared some candid thoughts about Apple's upcoming iPhone Duo.


The ‌iPhone Duo‌ uses a matte nano-texture display, which is meant to cut down on glare and minimize the visibility of the crease. When asked if the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s crease would be more visible over time, as that's what tends to happen on other foldables, Marieb said the nano-texture display would help. He asked people to hold the company "accountable" on crease visibility.

Marieb also discussed the Duo's innovative hinge, the use of Ceramic Shield 2 on the front display, and more.

Beats 360 Deliver Customizability and a Revamped Over-Ear Headphone Design

After months of teases and leaks, Apple's Beats brand officially announced its new Beats 360 headphone this week. Priced at $349.99, Beats 360 represents a rethinking of the Beats over-ear headphone design, with an emphasis on sound quality, comfort, and customizability.


Beats 360 is not a replacement for the brand's Studio Pro over-ear headphone, as the Studio Pro will remain part of the Beats lineup at a reduced price point of $299.99, down from the previous $349.99. Compared to Studio Pro, Beats 360 features a completely new acoustic architecture that delivers up to 1.75× more active noise cancellation and a 12dB increase in output while maintaining clarity across all frequencies with low distortion.

extra cushion kits at heavily discounted prices as part of a launch promo.

iPhone 20 Pro Display Sizes Leak Ahead of 2027 Launch

Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone lineup coming next year could feature slightly larger displays than the iPhone 18 Pro models, if a recent leak shared on Weibo is accurate.


Prolific Chinese leaker Digital Chat Station claims that early iPhone 20 Pro display specifications include a 6.41-inch screen with a resolution of approximately 2,686 × 1,236 pixels, while the iPhone 20 Pro Max is said to have a 6.96-inch display with a resolution of around 2,912 × 1,340 pixels.

For comparison, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature 6.27 inches (rounded to 6.3 inches) and 6.86 inches (rounded to 6.9 inches) respectively. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max resolutions are 2,622 × 1,206 pixels and 2,868 × 1,320 pixels, respectively.

title: Best iPhone 18 cases for iPhone 18 Pro & 18 Pro Max
content:
Macworld





You waited months for Apple’s new iPhones to arrive, but it’s worth protecting that investment from day one. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are tougher than previous generations, but they can still be scratched, chipped or damaged in a drop. A good case also does more than protect your phone: it can improve grip, add a stand or wallet, support MagSafe accessories and give your iPhone a completely different look.
There are hundreds of iPhone cases to choose from, ranging from inexpensive silicone shells to rugged cases built for serious drop protection. Price isn’t always a reliable guide to quality, either: a cheap case can split, yellow or develop faulty buttons, while spending more doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll get the best case for your needs.
That’s why we test and compare as many iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cases as we can. We consider protection, materials, build quality, grip, raised screen and camera edges, MagSafe compatibility, weight, useful extras such as stands and card storage, and how the case feels in everyday use. Where manufacturers make specific drop-protection claims, we include those too so you can compare different levels of protection.
In this guide we’ve grouped our recommendations into clear, colorful, protective and leather or faux-leather cases, with options at a range of prices. 
Best clear cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
Best fun cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
Best protective cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
Best leather cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max


Which type of iPhone case to choose
Apple gives you a handful of finishes; a case gives you thousands—an easy way to make an iPhone 18 Pro look like yours. You can choose a clear case that shows off the iPhone’s original color but adds vital protection, or choose a case with more personality. Protection is key, and some cases will add higher levels of defense than others.
Beyond looks, think about how you use your phone. Want hands-free video? Look for a case with a built-in stand. Want to leave your wallet at home? Choose one with card storage. And if you charge wirelessly, check for MagSafe compatibility — most cases now offer it, and it’s worth confirming before you buy.


						

							




Best clear cases for iPhone 18
If you want to keep your iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max looking like Apple intended you could leave it unprotected without a case, or simply choose a clear case that shows off the iPhone’s color while protecting it from everyday knocks and drops.

The Apple Clear Case is made from a blend of optically clear polycarbonate and other flexible materials, with a scratch-resistant coating on both the inside and outside. Zagg has a whole range of popular scratch-resistant clear case models for the iPhone 18 Pro series, including the Crystal Palace Snap, available with and without a kickstand) and a simpler Lite option without MagSafe and lower but still impressive drop protection. Zagg’s ClearGuard tech reduces the yellowing that affects many clear cases surprisingly quickly.
The Crystal Palace Snap ($54.99 / £39.99 with kickstand, $49.99 / £34.99 without) has textured sides for better grip, MagSafe, and 13ft drop protection. The Crystal Palace Lite Snap ($39.99 / £24.99) has MagSafe, 10ft drop protection and no kickstand. The entry-level Crystal Palace Lite ($29.99/ £19.99) lacks MagSafe and kickstand but still offers 10ft drop protection.
Both use PC and TPU, but the construction is fundamentally different. The premium Crystal Palace Snap uses a single, solid piece of PC across the back and sides to create a harder, more scratch-resistant clear case, with TPU used strategically so that there are no seams between the back and sides. The Lite version uses significantly more TPU, relying on a PC back plate combined with flexible, TPU sides. That makes it lighter and less expensive, but more susceptible to yellowing over time than PC.
If clear is sort of what you want but still a bit boring, Zagg adds metallic accents to its the Graphene-fortified Zagg Santa Cruz ($59.99 / £44.99 with kickstand, $54.99 / £39.99 without), giving the clear case an elegant edge and vibrancy with 13ft drop protection, MagSafe and kickstand.

 FAQ 


1.
What is Apple’s Ceramic Shield protection for iPhones?
Apple introduced Ceramic Shield with the iPhone 12 in 2020, developed jointly with glassmaker Corning, and it’s been standard on every iPhone since (excluding the budget SE line).
It’s made by fusing nano-ceramic crystals into glass, then dipping it in molten salt so potassium ions swap places with smaller sodium ions, creating a compressive surface layer that resists cracking. This gave the original iPhone 12 four times better drop performance than the iPhone 11.
Ceramic Shield 2 arrived with the iPhone 17 lineup in 2025, keeping the same crystal-infusion and ion-exchange process but with a refined composition that’s roughly three times more scratch-resistant than the first generation, while retaining similar drop protection. The Pro and Max models of the iPhone 17 and 18 also have Ceramic Shield 2 added to the back of the device.





2.
Why do you need an iPhone case?
Your iPhone is a precision device that lives in an unpredictable world—pockets, bags, countertops, pavement. A case is what stands between an accidental drop and a cracked screen or shattered back. It’s not a small risk either: plenty of new iPhone owners crack a screen within the first ten weeks of ownership (source). The IP68 rating means real dust and water resistance, but that’s a lab result—real life is messier. Add in the daily wear of being pulled in and out of a pocket, plus UV exposure over time, and the damage adds up quietly. A case won’t make your iPhone indestructible, but it absorbs the everyday hits so you don’t end up paying for a repair — or a replacement.





3.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro fit a case for the iPhone 17 Pro?
The iPhone 18 Pro series are virtually identical to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Even my iPhone 16 Pro fits in an 18 Pro case, and it works just fine—it looks a bit weird at the back, but otherwise fits nicely. On the other hand, a 17 Pro or 18 Pro wouldn’t fit in a 16 Pro case because of the rear camera positioning. Rokform told Macworld that its iPhone 18 Pro case lineup is compatible with iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro models. However, its older iPhone 17 Pro case lineup is not compatible with iPhone 18 models due to camera plateau design differences. Cases designed with tight tolerances might therefore have a problem as the camera plateau on iPhone 18 Pro/Max is about 0.5mm taller than on iPhone 17 Pro/Max.
Leading case manufacturer OtterBox reports that its iPhone 18 Pro/Max cases are “also compatible with iPhone 17 Pro, so the cases can be used interchangeably between those two models”.
New cases are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection, so buying a case built specifically for your iPhone model is the safest option. Check our roundup of the Best iPhone 17 Cases and Best iPhone 16 Cases for the older models.





4.
Do I need a screen protector if I use a case?
Yes, it’s still worth using a screen protector even if you have a case, as the two provide different but complementary protection. A case protects the back, corners, and edges of your iPhone, while a screen protector is designed to protect the display itself from scratches and cracks. 
Tempered-glass screen protectors can help absorb direct impacts and protect against everyday scratches and abrasions. A case with a raised lip offers some protection if your iPhone lands face down, but it can’t prevent every object or surface from making direct contact with the screen.





5.
What type of iPhone case offers the best protection?
When it comes to maximum protection for your iPhone, the clear winners are rugged cases built with multi-layer materials and military-grade drop ratings. Rugged cases typically combine a hard polycarbonate outer shell with a shock-absorbing TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) inner layer, reinforced corners, and raised edges around both the screen and camera to prevent direct surface contact on drops.
While silicone and leather cases offer decent everyday scratch protection, they simply can’t match the impact resistance of a purpose-built rugged case.
When choosing a protective case, look for:
Raised lip around the front (at least 1mm) to keep the screen safely off surfaces.
Raised camera edge (0.5mm minimum, some go up to 3.6mm).
MIL-STD-810G certification — a U.S. Department of Defense standard for durability.
Reinforced corners for impact absorption.
MagSafe compatibility if you wirelessly charge.





6.
Do I need an iPhone case for iPhone 18?
Many consumers damage their devices each year, with cracked, chipped or shattered screens the leading reason for iPhone repairs. A screen protector is an important first line of defense, but a case with a raised edge can much better protect the display from everyday knocks and drops, and tough sides and back will reduce the risk of damage from an accidental fall.
Ceramic Shield 2, introduced with the iPhone 17 generation, protects the front of the iPhone 18 Pro and offers three times better scratch resistance than the iPhone 16 Pro. The back uses Ceramic Shield, which Apple says offers four times better crack resistance than the back glass used on earlier models.
The 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are the best-protected iPhones yet, but a case is still worth buying. It helps keep that pristine finish looking new and, when it’s time to trade up, a well-protected iPhone can retain far more resale value than the cost of the case itself.





How we test iPhone cases
When we receive new cases, we test them for fit, button feel, grip, MagSafe strength and alignment, raised-edge camera and screen protection, bulk, weight, and day-to-day handling. Where we are unable to test a case ourselves, we assess it based on its specifications and our experience with other cases from the same manufacturer that have impressed us. We report manufacturers’ claimed drop-protection metrics. As we have listed iPhone cases only from trusted companies we feel safe in these claims but note that measurement is the maker’s own and not ours or Apple’s.

title: This $30 AI storage cleanup app saves you from buying more cloud space
content:
Macworld





TL;DR: Cleaner Kit for iOS is an AI-powered cleanup app for photos, videos, contacts, and email, and a lifetime Premium Plan subscription is on sale for $29.99 (reg. $104.97).
An iPhone fills up fast with duplicate photos, blurry screenshots, and old emails nobody needs anymore. Cleaner Kit for iOS clears all of that with AI-powered scanning, and a lifetime Premium Plan subscription is on sale for $29.99 (reg. $104.97).
Camera roll scans catch duplicate and low-quality photos and videos, and a swipe right keeps a shot while a swipe left archives it for later deletion. Video compression shrinks file sizes without a visible drop in quality.
Contacts get merged and cleaned of empty or unnamed entries, and Gmail’s inbox sorts by sender, so old messages clear out in bulk rather than one at a time. title: watchOS 27: 12 New Things To Check Out on Your Apple Watch
content:
Apple released watchOS 27 on September 14. The features and changes aren't limited to owners of new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 models. If you have an Apple Watch model that supports the latest update, here are 12 features and changes to check out after installation.


To do so, open the Watch app on your iPhone, then tap General ➝ Software Update, strap your watch into a charger, and follow the onscreen prompts.

Check Out the Dedicated Siri App


Siri has finally caught up with the AI revolution, and apart from having contextual awareness, it now has an app of its own that collects every conversation in a single view and syncs them privately across your devices over iCloud. Just ask something on your iPhone and you can pick the thread up again on your Apple Watch, as well as pin conversations worth keeping, or even start a new chat directly from your wrist.

Try Siri Modular Watch Face


The new Siri watch face is a genuinely useful one. Its rectangular complication shows you whatever sits at the top of your Smart Stack, and it automatically updates through the day based on time, location, and other factors.

The Dynamic App Grid


Pressing the Digital Crown no longer produces the honeycomb app view by default. Now, watchOS 27 shows a dynamic grid made up of suggested apps, your most-used apps, and your most recently used ones. The Siri app sits in the middle, but the alphabetical list remains available – simply turn the Digital Crown to navigate through all of your apps.

New Tap Gesture


Apple has added a third gesture to Double Tap and Wrist Flick. The new one is simply called Tap. A single tap of your index finger and thumb opens the highlighted widget in the Smart Stack. You can still navigate the Smart Stack with Double Tap and dismiss notifications with Wrist Flick.

Walkie-Talkie Has Been Deleted


Walkie-Talkie is gone, and not merely hidden. The app is unavailable after updating to watchOS 27 and cannot be reinstalled from the App Store. You can keep the app by staying on watchOS 26, but you won't be able to start a conversation with a contact who has updated.

Live Rewind (Not Yet)


This is the change most likely to catch people out. In watchOS 26 and earlier, a double press of the Digital Crown opens the App Switcher, where you can jump back to the previous app, scroll through recent ones, and swipe to force-quit anything misbehaving.

That's changed in watchOS 27, in which a double press shows the new dynamic app grid instead. The gesture has been reserved for Live Rewind, an upcoming feature (exclusive to Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4) that produces a transcript of the last fifteen seconds of speech in your environment. 

Fortunately, the App Switcher will still be available when watchOS 27.2 is released later this year, but it will open with a different gesture. If you're already on the latest beta, simply long press on the bottom of the app that you're in, and that should open the App Switcher.

Find My is Now One App


Find Devices, Find Items, and Find People have been folded into a single Find My app with a map-centric layout, which also includes shortcuts for directions and for items nearby. 

Workout Buddy No Longer Needs Your iPhone


Introduced in watchOS 26, Workout Buddy previously required your iPhone within range. In watchOS 27, your Apple Watch can run it if Wi-Fi or cellular is available. It also draws new insights from your training history, tracking gradual gains in pace, distance and workout duration, and it now speaks Spanish as well as English.

New Cycle Tracking Features


Cycle Tracking in the Health app can now notify you if your logged patterns are suggestive of perimenopause, alongside symptom tracking and educational material. The notifications only draw on your logged cycle history and apply to users aged 40 and over. Apple says the feature is not a method of birth control and is not a diagnosis.

Treadmill Distance Is More Accurate


In watchOS 27, new machine learning motion algorithms measure distance more precisely for indoor runs and walks, and Apple says the improvement starts from the first step, as opposed to settling after a few minutes. Fitness route maps are more accurate too, and step counts finally stay in sync between the Fitness and Health apps.

The Smart Stack Gets More to Say


The Smart Stack's contextual suggestions are now a lot smarter. A few examples provided by Apple include new widgets surfacing your parked car's location, a close contact's birthday, a change in your transit card balance, the Noise app immediately after a loud-noise alert, a reminder that Theater Mode is still on, pinned messages, celebrations, and identity cards.

New Models Get a Steps Counter

title: Banks and Credit Unions to Team Up Against Apple Pay Fees
content:
An antitrust lawsuit accusing Apple of blocking tap-to-pay competition is moving forward and will see banks and credit unions able to band together to sue Apple.


U.S. District Judge Jeffrey White this week certified a class in the lawsuit. It will include any U.S. entities that issued any payment card enabled for Apple Pay and paid Apple a fee for ‌Apple Pay‌ transactions on that payment card. He also denied a motion from Apple to exclude expert testimony that plaintiff attorneys allege offers proof Apple has monopoly power over the mobile wallet market.

First filed in 2022, the suit claims Apple illegally collects up to $1 billion annually in fees by preventing rivals from accessing the iPhone's NFC chip to build mobile wallets that would compete with ‌Apple Pay‌. When an iPhone user buys something with a card linked to ‌Apple Pay‌, the card issuer has to pay Apple a 0.15 percent fee for credit cards and half a cent for debit cards, according to the lawsuit. If you make a $1,000 purchase via ‌Apple Pay‌, Apple collects $1.50 from the card issuer.

The complaint alleges that Apple forces card issuers to pay fees by making ‌Apple Pay‌ the only tap-to-pay option. It points to Google's Android, which supports multiple wallets and does not collect a fee from card issuers for contactless payments. It suggests Apple would not be able to continue to charge "substantial fees" if it were forced to support other mobile wallets on Apple devices.

As of iOS 18.1, developers are able to offer NFC contactless payments in their apps. Developers have access to the NFC chip in the United States, Canada, Australia, Brazil, Japan, New Zealand, the UK, the European Economic Area, and many other countries.

title: 2026 iPad mini: Release date, OLED display, A19 Pro, price and latest rumors
content:
Macworld





For those who need a premium small-screen tablet, the iPad mini is a popular choice. But should you buy one now, or should you wait to see what Apple has in store for the next model? 
Most buyers should wait – the next model is expected to bring meaningful upgrades. However, Apple isn’t expected to update the iPad mini until late 2026 or maybe even early 2027, and that launch date could slip further due to chip demand and wider supply constraints.
Here’s what the latest rumors say about the release date, key upgrades, and whether it’s worth waiting. 
2026 iPad mini: Rumored changes at a glance
A20 Pro chip possible
OLED display upgrade
Screen size could increase from 8.3-inch to 8.5- or 8.7-inches
More water-resistant design
Vibration-based speaker system
Price increase
Improved connectivity 
iPad mini 7 vs iPad mini 8 comparison


FeatureCurrent iPad miniRumoured next iPad mini

ReleaseOctober 2024Late 2026 / early 2027
ChipA17 ProLikely A19 Pro; A18 Pro/A20 Pro possible
Display8.3-inch LCDOLED, possibly 8.5 inches
DesignCurrent designSimilar design, possibly slimmer bezels
Water resistanceNo official ratingImproved resistance rumoured
WirelessWi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread
Cellular modemQualcommApple C1X expected
Cameras12MP front and rearSimilar cameras; landscape front camera is rumored
Apple IntelligenceSupportedSupported, with faster AI performance
PriceFrom $599 (was $499)Unknown; OLED could push price higher
Biggest upgrade—OLED display, faster chip and newer connectivity

 






2026 iPad mini release date: When will the new iPad mini launch?
Late 2026/early 2027
Apple has not officially announced a launch date for the next iPad mini. Earlier reports pointed to a release before the end of 2026, but more recent reporting leaves open the possibility that it could slip into early 2027. 
Back in October 2025, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that a new iPad mini with an OLED display was among the devices Apple expected to launch before the end of 2026. Then, in July 2026, he narrowed that down further, reporting that the OLED iPad mini was scheduled for an October 2026 release.
However, in September 2026 Gurman included the iPad mini in a broader list of products expected to ship in late 2026 or early 2027, introducing some uncertainty around the exact timing.
There is still strong evidence that the new model is approaching. References to an upcoming iPad mini have reportedly been found in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, while Samsung Display is said to have begun mass production of OLED panels for the device.
In September, a report from MacRumors said could be coming soon. Based on a leak from “Apple’s own code,” a new iPad mini could arrive next month.
The iPad mini also has a relatively unpredictable release cycle, with Apple sometimes leaving several years between updates. Wider component constraints, including pressure on RAM and other parts highlighted by Apple CEO Tim Cook earlier in 2026, could also affect the schedule, although there is no firm evidence that these have delayed the iPad mini specifically.


						

							


2026 iPad mini chip: Performance and specs 
A20 Pro or A19 Pro chip
C1X modem
N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6
Since it hasn’t been updated in over a year, the next iPad mini is expected to receive several silicon upgrades. The current model features an A17 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, and Apple Intelligence support, while most rumors point to the new model adopting the A19 Pro..
In August 2025, MacRumors reported that Apple code appeared to reveal an A19 Pro-powered iPad mini. Further evidence emerged in December 2025, when Macworld reported internal Apple code indicating that the entry-level iPad would move to an A19 chip. Since Apple has traditionally given the iPad mini a more powerful processor than the standard iPad, that strengthens the case for the A19 Pro.
An A19 Pro would represent a substantial upgrade over the current A17 Pro. Users could expect faster on-device AI processing, improved gaming performance, and quicker photo and video editing. The A18 Pro, which powers the MacBook Neo, is often compared to the M1 chip and can rival the M3 in some single-core workloads. An A19 Pro-powered iPad mini would push the device even closer to iPad Air-level performance.
An A19 Pro would deliver a substantial performance boost over the A17 Pro, particularly for on-device AI, gaming, and photo and video editing, while bringing the iPad mini closer to iPad Air-level performance.
There have also been suggestions that Apple could use either the A18 Pro or A20 Pro, depending on timing and chip availability. According to a report from MacRumors based on a leak from “Apple’s own code,” a new iPad mini could feature an A20 Pro chip, which made its debut with the iPhone 18 Pro.
Alongside the processor upgrade, Apple is expected to bring its latest wireless technologies to the iPad mini. The N1 chip, introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup, supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and is expected to spread across the iPad lineup. Cellular models are also expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem.
Alongside processor upgrades, Apple is expected to bring its latest wireless technologies to the iPad mini. The N1 chip, introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup, supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and is expected to spread across the iPad lineup. Cellular models are also expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Display
OLED display upgrade

				
					

				
			
The M4 iPad Pro’s OLED Display could make its way to the iPad mini next.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The biggest display upgrade rumored for the next iPad mini is the adoption of OLED technology. Following Apple’s transition of the iPad Pro to OLED in 2024, multiple reports have suggested that the iPad mini will be the next iPad to make the switch. Ross Young of DSCC was first to claim, in a tweet in October 2024, that the next iPad mini would have a OLED. 
The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, still uses a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display, but industry sources, including Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, indicate a move to OLED is increasingly likely.
The transition from LCD to OLED would represent one of the most significant upgrades in the iPad mini’s history. Unlike LCD panels, which rely on a backlight, OLED displays illuminate each pixel individually. This allows pixels to switch off completely when displaying black content, resulting in deeper blacks, higher contrast ratios, and improved HDR performance.
Key benefits of OLED include:
Superior contrast and true blacks: Individual pixel control allows OLED displays to produce true blacks and extremely high contrast.
More vibrant colours: OLED can make images appear more vivid and punchy, particularly in high-contrast scenes and HDR content.
Faster response times: Quicker pixel response can reduce motion blur and ghosting when gaming or watching fast-moving video.
Better viewing angles: Colours and contrast remain more consistent when the display is viewed from the side.
Potential efficiency benefits: OLED can use less power when displaying darker content and can enable thinner display assemblies, although bright screens may consume more power, so battery-life gains aren’t guaranteed.
An OLED panel could also enable Apple to reduce bezel sizes, potentially increasing the display area slightly without significantly changing the tablet’s overall dimensions. Some reports suggest the screen could grow from 8.3 inches to around 8.5 inches as a result – more on that below.
While the iPad mini is unlikely to inherit premium display technologies such as ProMotion or the tandem OLED architecture used in the iPad Pro, the move to OLED would still deliver a noticeable improvement in visual quality, with richer blacks, better contrast, improved colour reproduction, and stronger HDR performance.
For users who prioritise display quality, an OLED iPad mini would address one of the most frequently cited limitations of the current model and bring the compact tablet much closer to the viewing experience offered by Apple’s premium devices.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Design
Same size, bigger screen possible
More water-resistant design rumored

				
					

				
			
Apple




The iPad mini has retained the same design since its major redesign in 2021, and the 2026 model is expected to keep that overall look. However, Apple could increase the display size slightly while maintaining the device’s current dimensions.
In December 2024, analysts at Display Supply Chain Consultants (DSCC) suggested in a supply chain analyst report that the next-generation iPad mini could feature an 8.5-inch display, up from the current model’s 8.3-inch panel. The reports indicated that the chassis size would remain unchanged, meaning Apple could achieve the larger screen through slimmer bezels rather than a larger body.
A larger display may also help the iPad mini maintain its place in Apple’s lineup as foldable devices arrive. Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone – often referred to as the iPhone Fold or iPhone Ultra – is expected to feature an inner display measuring between 7.6 and 7.8 inches with a 4:3 aspect ratio, putting it close to the iPad mini’s screen size. While still smaller than the iPad mini, such a device could appeal to some users who currently favour Apple’s smallest tablet. 
Another rumor gaining traction is that the new iPad mini will be more water-resistant. That rumor comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who in October 2025 claimed Apple was developing a next-generation iPad mini with a significantly more water-resistant chassis. 
The design changes could include: 
Redesigned casing with improved sealing around ports. 
According to Gurman, a new speaker system could use vibration-based audio technology to eliminate traditional speaker holes.
There’s also a strong possibility of new colour options. Apple currently offers the iPad mini in Blue, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray, while the previous generation was available in Pink, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Cameras 
Little or no camera upgrade expected

				
					

				
			
Apple is not expected to upgrade the cameras in the next iPad mini.

Foundry




The current iPad mini has a 12MP Wide rear camera and 12MP Ultra Wide Center Stage front camera, and there are no credible reports suggesting major camera system upgrades for the next iPad mini.
The most likely change concerns camera placement rather than camera hardware. Apple has moved the front-facing camera to the landscape edge on its latest iPad models, and the iPad mini could follow suit to improve the experience during video calls and FaceTime sessions when used with a keyboard or stand.
According to a September report from MacRumors based on a leak from “Apple’s own code,” a new iPad mini will include a landscape front-facing camera.
While the cameras themselves may remain unchanged, image quality could still benefit from improvements to the image signal processor and computational photography capabilities of a newer A-series chip.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Price 
The iPad mini had held the same $499/£499 starting price since its 2021 redesign. That changed in June 2026, when Apple increased the entry-level price to $599/£599.
With Apple having already raised the price this year, we think another increase with the next iPad mini is unlikely, although the move to OLED could put some pressure on costs.


						

							


Should I wait to buy a new iPad mini? 
The current iPad mini’s A17 Pro chip is still plenty fast for everyday use, gaming and creative apps. An OLED display could make the next model significantly more appealing, but its launch timing remains uncertain. With discounts likely on the current model, buy now if you value portability and performance; wait if display quality matters most.

title: Is a cellular Apple Watch worth it? GPS vs Cellular explained
content:
Macworld





Do you really need an Apple Watch with cellular? Apple’s GPS + Cellular models let you make calls, send messages, stream music and use online services when your iPhone isn’t nearby, but you’ll pay more for the Watch and usually need an additional cellular plan.
For many Apple Watch owners, the standard GPS model is all they need because their iPhone is rarely far away. But cellular can make a big difference if you regularly run, work out, walk the dog or go out without your phone, or if you want an Apple Watch for a child or family member who doesn’t have an iPhone.
Apple’s current lineup consists of the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch SE 3. The Series 12 and SE 3 are available in GPS and GPS + Cellular versions, while every Apple Watch Ultra 4 includes cellular connectivity.
So is a cellular Apple Watch worth paying extra for? Here’s what you get, what you don’t, and who should choose each version.
Apple Watch GPS vs GPS + Cellular – At a glance


FeatureGPS Apple WatchGPS + Cellular Apple Watch

GPS workout tracking without iPhoneYesYes
Apple Pay without iPhoneYesYes
Downloaded music and podcasts without iPhoneYesYes
Calls and messages with iPhone nearbyYesYes
Calls and messages without iPhoneOver Wi-FiYes, with Wi-Fi or an active cellular plan
Stream music without iPhoneWi-Fi requiredYes, with Wi-Fi or cellular
Receive internet-based notifications away from iPhoneWi-Fi requiredYes, with Wi-Fi or cellular
Emergency calling away from iPhoneRequires Wi-Fi or another supported connectionCellular provides an additional connection
Apple Watch For Your KidsNoYes
Additional hardware costNoYes
Monthly cellular feeNoUsually
Potential battery impact from cellular useNo cellular radio useYes, particularly during extended direct cellular use

 






Apple Watch GPS vs GPS + Cellular: What’s the difference?
The biggest difference is simple: a GPS + Cellular Apple Watch can connect directly to a mobile network when your iPhone isn’t with you and Wi-Fi isn’t available.
A GPS-only Apple Watch doesn’t need your iPhone to use GPS. Both versions can record workouts and collect GPS data when you’re running, cycling or walking without your phone, and the information syncs with your iPhone when the devices reconnect.
A GPS Apple Watch can also use Apple Pay, monitor your health and play downloaded music, podcasts and audiobooks without an iPhone or internet connection. If it connects to a compatible Wi-Fi network, it can also use many internet-based features while your iPhone is out of range.
The extra cellular connection is primarily useful when you want to make and receive calls, send messages, stream audio or use apps that need an internet connection when neither your iPhone nor a usable Wi-Fi network is available.


						

							




Which Apple Watches have cellular in 2026

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Apple’s current lineup consists of the Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
The Apple Watch Series 12 and SE 3 require you to make the GPS-versus-cellular decision when you buy. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn’t: cellular hardware is included as standard.


Apple WatchGPS priceGPS + Cellular priceCellular difference

Apple Watch SE 3, 40mm$249/£219$299/£289$50/£70
Apple Watch Series 12, 42mm$399/£369$499/£469$100/£100
Apple Watch Ultra 4, 49mm—$799/£749Cellular included

 Prices shown are Apple’s starting prices and can vary with case size, material and band.






What can a cellular Apple Watch do without an iPhone?
The main reason to buy a cellular Apple Watch is that it can remain connected when you leave your iPhone behind.
With a Wi-Fi or cellular connection you can:
Make and receive phone calls.
Send and receive messages.
Receive notifications.
Stream Apple Music, podcasts and audiobooks.
Read email.
Use Maps.
Use apps and services that require an internet connection.
You don’t need cellular for everything, though.
Away from your iPhone, a GPS Apple Watch can still track workouts and activity, collect GPS data, monitor health, use Apple Pay and play music, podcasts and audiobooks stored on the Watch.
That distinction is important. You don’t need cellular simply because you want to go running without your iPhone. A GPS Apple Watch can still record your run.
Cellular becomes useful if you also want to receive calls and messages, stream rather than download your music, use Maps and other online services, or remain contactable while your iPhone is at home.
Of course, if you use cellular on your Apple Watch to do those things you will have to pay for the data.
For more information read: All the things an Apple Watch can do without an iPhone.


						

							




Who should buy a cellular Apple Watch – and who shouldn’t?
If you’re unsure which version to buy, it mainly comes down to how often you expect to use your Apple Watch without your iPhone.
For most people, the key question is: How often will you actually use your Apple Watch away from your iPhone and a Wi-Fi connection?
If that’s a regular part of how you expect to use the Watch, cellular can be worth the extra cost. If your iPhone rarely leaves your side, the GPS model provides most of the same everyday Apple Watch experience for less.


If this sounds like you…Choose
You regularly run, cycle, exercise or go out without your iPhone and still want calls, messages, Maps, streaming and notificationsGPS + Cellular
You specifically want to carry your iPhone less but remain contactableGPS + Cellular
You want an additional way to contact emergency services when your iPhone and Wi-Fi aren’t availableGPS + Cellular
You’re buying an Apple Watch for a child or family member without their own iPhoneGPS + Cellular
You’re buying an Apple Watch Ultra 4Cellular is included; decide whether you need to activate a plan
Your iPhone is almost always with youGPS
You mainly want health, fitness and workout trackingGPS
You’re happy to download music and podcasts before exercisingGPS
Keeping the purchase price and ongoing costs as low as possible is your priorityGPS

 






Why you might want an Apple Watch with cellular

				
					

				
			
Thomas Deehan / Foundry




The main reason to buy an Apple Watch with cellular is the freedom to leave your iPhone behind while staying fully connected. 
Here are the most compelling use cases:
You exercise without your iPhone
Running, cycling, swimming and going to the gym are among the clearest use cases for a cellular Apple Watch.
You can leave your iPhone at home but still make or receive a call, get messages and notifications, stream music and use connected services.
Without cellular, you can still track your workout and listen to downloaded music. If you connect to a known Wi-Fi network, you can also access many online features.
The advantage of cellular is that you aren’t dependent on finding Wi-Fi.
You regularly leave your phone behind
Cellular makes sense if one of the reasons you’re buying an Apple Watch is to carry your iPhone less.
You might want to go for a walk, head to the gym, walk the dog or run an errand without taking your phone while still remaining contactable.
If your iPhone is almost always in your pocket or bag, however, the Watch will normally use its connection instead, making the cellular hardware largely redundant.
You want connectivity for emergencies
Cellular can also provide reassurance when you’re exercising or walking without your iPhone.
Fall Detection and Crash Detection can detect an incident without an iPhone, but the Watch requires a network connection to contact emergency services. A cellular Watch can use its own mobile connection when Wi-Fi isn’t available.
There is an important exception with the Ultra 4. The Ultra 4 also has satellite connectivity and supports Emergency SOS and Find My location sharing via satellite when cellular and Wi-Fi aren’t available.
The Series 12 does not have built-in satellite connectivity.
You’re setting up an Apple Watch for a child
A cellular model is also the right choice when setting up an Apple Watch for a child or another family member who doesn’t have their own iPhone.
Apple Watch For Your Kids, previously called Family Setup, allows a family member’s Apple Watch to be configured from another person’s iPhone. A cellular plan allows calls, messages and location sharing when the Watch is away from the managing iPhone.
This makes the cellular SE 3 an attractive option for children because it’s Apple’s least expensive current Apple Watch. 


						

							


Why you might not need a cellular Apple Watch
For a large number of Apple Watch owners, their iPhone is almost always nearby.
When your iPhone is in your pocket or bag, your Apple Watch can already use its connection for calls, messages, notifications and internet access. You aren’t gaining much from the Watch’s cellular hardware during that time.
And even when your iPhone isn’t nearby, your Apple Watch can use known Wi-Fi networks for many online features.
There are also plenty of things that don’t require either cellular or Wi-Fi. You can track workouts and activity, collect GPS data, monitor your health, use Apple Pay and play downloaded media.
So ask yourself how often you actually expect to leave your iPhone behind.
If the answer is “hardly ever,” paying more for the cellular Watch and paying your network provider a monthly fee is unlikely to offer much practical benefit.
For more help deciding which Apple Watch to buy read our guide to the best Apple Watch.


						

							


Does cellular use more Apple Watch battery?

				
					

				
			
Jim Martin / Foundry




Yes. Cellular connectivity can drain an Apple Watch battery faster, particularly when you’re using the Watch independently of your iPhone for extended periods.
Apple itself says battery life varies according to cellular coverage. We’ve also found in previous Apple Watch testing that battery life is affected by how much cellular connectivity you use. That’s because an Apple Watch is most power-efficient when it’s connected to its paired iPhone over Bluetooth. When the iPhone isn’t available, Wi-Fi uses less power than a mobile network.
Signal strength matters too. Apple advises connecting to a strong Wi-Fi or cellular signal where possible because maintaining a connection in an area with poor coverage can consume more battery power.
That means activities such as making calls, streaming music or using online apps over cellular for long periods are likely to have a greater impact than receiving the occasional message or notification.
Buying a GPS + Cellular model doesn’t mean the Watch will constantly use its mobile connection, however. Apple Watch automatically chooses the most power-efficient available connection: Bluetooth to your iPhone first, followed by Wi-Fi and then cellular when the other connections aren’t available.
Interestingly, Apple has sometimes fitted cellular versions of a Watch with a larger battery than the equivalent GPS model. The 44mm first-generation Apple Watch SE, for example, had a 1.129Wh battery in its cellular version compared with 0.994Wh in the GPS model. This hasn’t been consistent across Apple Watch generations, however, and many later GPS and cellular models have used identical-capacity batteries.
Apple rates the Series 12 for up to 24 hours of normal use and the Ultra 4 for up to 50 hours, while the SE 3 is rated for up to 18 hours.
We’ve also seen much better real-world results from the Series 12. In our first full battery test, the Series 12 lasted 51 hours before running out of power. However, battery life varies significantly according to how the Watch is used, and this wasn’t a test of sustained cellular use.
If you’re trying to extend battery life, Low Power Mode can help. When your iPhone isn’t nearby, Low Power Mode normally turns off Wi-Fi and cellular connections along with incoming calls and notifications. If you open an app that requires data, however, the Watch can temporarily reconnect so the app works.
If you expect to spend many hours away from your iPhone making calls, streaming or using data over cellular, battery life should therefore be a more significant consideration when choosing between GPS and GPS + Cellular.
If maximum battery endurance matters more to you than remaining connected when your iPhone isn’t nearby, the GPS-only model removes cellular as a potential source of additional power consumption.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Can you use an Apple Watch without paying for cellular?
Yes. A GPS Apple Watch doesn’t require a cellular plan, and you can also use a GPS + Cellular model without activating cellular service.
Without cellular, the Watch can use your iPhone’s connection or Wi-Fi for online features. It can also perform many tasks without an internet connection at all, including tracking workouts and activity, monitoring health, using Apple Pay and playing downloaded media.
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 includes cellular hardware as standard, but that doesn’t mean you have to activate a cellular plan.





2.
Can a cellular Apple Watch make calls without an iPhone nearby?
Yes.
When connected to its cellular network, a GPS + Cellular Apple Watch can make and receive calls without its paired iPhone nearby.
A GPS Apple Watch can also make calls without the iPhone nearby if it has a suitable Wi-Fi connection.





3.
Do I need the same carrier for my iPhone and Apple Watch?
No, you don’t need the same carrier for your iPhone and Apple Watch, but there are some important practical considerations to keep in mind.
A cellular Apple Watch can work with a different carrier than your iPhone, but the setup is more complicated. In most cases, carriers offer Apple Watch plans that are designed to work in conjunction with an existing wireless phone plan. 





4.
Can I buy a cellular Apple Watch now and activate cellular later?
Yes. You don’t have to activate cellular service when you buy a GPS + Cellular Apple Watch.
The Ultra 4 is a good example: every Ultra 4 contains cellular hardware, but you don’t have to activate a mobile plan. 





How much does a cellular Apple Watch cost? 
A cellular Apple Watch Series 11 costs $100/$100 more than the standard version, while the SE costs $50/£70 more if you want to include cellular. The Apple Watch Ultra is only available with cellular.
Some networks will charge you extra to get data on your Apple Watch, while others allow you to add it to an existing iPhone contract and share the data.
A cellular Apple Watch plan typically costs about $10 per month in the U.S., on top of your existing wireless phone plan. This is the figure most commonly cited across carriers and deal coverage.
Here’s a breakdown of what to expect:
U.S. options: Most major U.S. carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, Xfinity Mobile, and others) charge around $10/month for unlimited data on an Apple Watch when paired with an existing iPhone plan. See Apple’s exhaustive list of providers. 
U.K. options: Carriers like Three, EE, O2, and Vodafone offer cellular Apple Watch plans. Notably, Three lets you connect your watch to your iPhone and share the existing data allowance at no additional cost through its Smartwatch Pairing Plan.
For more advice on buying an Apple Watch, take a look at our round-up of the best Apple Watch deals and our in-depth Apple Watch buying guide.

title: New HomePods likely coming soon with Siri AI, updated colors
content:
Macworld





Now that Siri AI is officially available in the OS 27 updates, Apple may be getting ready to finally release the updates to the HomePod and HomePod mini. A couple of new reports give us a peek at what we might see.
The first report comes from MacRumors. The site’s controbutor, Aaron Perris, spotted Apple code that refers to the new HomePod mini and icons that show the colors that will be available: black, blue, green, pink, and white. That means orange and yellow, which are in the current color lineup, will be dropped. According to the site’s images, the new blue is a lighter shade, and presumably, black and midnight are the same.
The second report comes via a post by itspdfu, who has a history of posting accurate leaks online. They report that audioOS27, the upcoming operating system for HomePod devices, supports Siri AI. In addition to Siri Ai support, the new HomePod will have new animations for the device’s display.


Get ready for Siri AI on HomePod. 
audioOS 27 includes Linwood, the system behind Siri AI, plus a new look and sound for Siri on HomePod. May require new hardware.
The new status lights emphasize white, blue and orange, matching Siri AI’s palette on other devices.
🔊 Sound on pic.twitter.com/jZKzLx946y
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 23, 2026





An alarming point in itspdfu’s report is that new hardware may be needed, which means that Siri AI would not be available of older HomePods. Apple released the original HomePod in 2018, and it had a three-year run before Apple paused production of the product. Then in 2023, Apple released an updated HomePod, which remains currently available for purchase.
Itspdfu’s report doesn’t mention the new HomePod mini specifically, though it’s long been rumored that the new HomePod mini will have Siri AI support as well. We’re also expecting a new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI support. None of the current devices support Apple Intelligence or the new Siri.
Apple is expected to make a big push into the smarthome market with the new HomePods and an new device that’s been dubbed a “home hub” that acts as a central control point. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has reported that Apple plans to release the new devices before the end of the year.

title: HomePod rumors: All we know about HomePod mini 2, HomePod Touch & HomePad hub
content:
Macworld





Apple’s HomePod lineup could be about to undergo its biggest expansion since the original HomePod launched. Rather than simply refreshing its existing smart speakers, Apple is reportedly preparing several new smart home devices, including products that blur the line between HomePod, smart display and home hub.
The company is said to have three smart home products “very nearly ready to release,” according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. However, Apple is reportedly delaying their launch until its redesigned AI-powered Siri is ready, with the new assistant expected to debut alongside the OS 27 updates later this year.
If those plans stay on track, Apple could unveil its next wave of HomePod and smart home devices shortly after iOS 27 and the upgraded Siri are released this fall.
In this guide, we round up all the latest rumours and reports about Apple’s upcoming HomePod products, including expected release dates, new hardware, Apple Intelligence features and pricing.


What are the new HomePod products?
Apple’s HomePod lineup currently consists of two models, both of which became more expensive following Apple’s June 2026 price increases. The HomePod mini now costs $129, while the 2nd-generation HomePod is priced at $349. But the real story isn’t the current speakers – it’s the next generation of smart home devices Apple is preparing.
According to multiple reports, Apple is developing several new HomePod-related products, including updated HomePod and HomePod mini models and a display-equipped smart home hub, widely referred to as the “HomePad.”
Rumored new products include the following, the names aren’t confirmed, we are using them as placeholders: 


						

							






Placeholder nameWhat is it When Likelihood 

HomePod mini 2Updated internals, faster chip, and new colors including redMid-202610/10
HomePod 3Updated internals, faster chipMid-202610/10
HomePod TouchHomePod with a built-in 6-7in touchscreenLate-20266/10
HomePadA smart display with a 6-7in screen possibly wall-mounted. To be the command centre of the home. Late-20266/10
HomeHubCombining a HomePod speaker, display, and advanced home-control features (building on HomePod Touch concept, may not be separate product)Late-20266/10
Screen mounted on robot arm Display mounted on a robotic arm (could be evolution of HomePod concept)2027 or beyond5/10
Security cameraA security camera is said to be part of Apple’s smart home roadmap2027 or beyond5/10

 






Why hasn’t Apple launched the new HomePod devices yet?
The biggest obstacle is Siri.
Apple’s next-generation Siri is designed to be a far more capable assistant, able to understand conversational context, personal information and on-screen content as part of Apple Intelligence. However, the chips inside today’s HomePods simply aren’t powerful enough to support these features.
The HomePod mini uses the Apple Watch S5 chip, while the 2nd-generation HomePod runs on the S7 chip. Those processors work well for music playback, HomeKit control and basic voice commands, but they lack the performance needed for Apple’s latest AI models.
As a result, Apple is widely believed to have delayed its new HomePod hardware until it can launch devices capable of delivering the full Siri AI experience. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that several smart home products are effectively ready, but are being held back until the redesigned Siri ships with the iOS 27 software updates later this year.
That means the next generation of HomePods is expected to feature significantly more powerful Apple silicon, enabling Apple Intelligence features that the current models cannot support.


						

							







HomePod mini 2
We’ll start off with the rumors about the HomePod mini 2. The HomePod mini is Apple’s smaller, more affordable smart speaker. The new model is expected to offer a new red color option, major processor upgrade and improved connectivity.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the HomePod mini 2 expected to launch?
October 2026
Apple introduced the original HomePod mini in November 2020, so it is now nearly six years old and overdue for an update.
Rumours of a successor have circulated for more than a year. In January 2025, reports suggested a launch toward the end of 2025, and Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman subsequently said that new HomePod mini and Apple TV models were expected in autumn 2025. Those products never materialised.
Attention then shifted to spring 2026, with reports suggesting Apple’s new smart home devices would launch alongside its redesigned Siri. However, that timetable also slipped as Apple continued work on its AI-powered assistant.
The latest reports now point to an October 2026 launch. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has several smart home products that are nearly ready but is waiting for the redesigned Siri to ship with the OS 27 updates before introducing new hardware.
If those plans remain on schedule, the HomePod mini 2 is expected to launch alongside Apple’s broader refresh of its smart home lineup this fall, with most reports pointing to October.
What changes are coming to the HomePod mini 2?
Black, blue, green, pink, and white.
The current HomePod mini is available in Midnight, White, Blue, Yellow and Orange. In September 2025, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple has tested additional colours for the next-generation model, including red, although it remains unclear whether any new colours will make it to the final product.
In September, MacRumors spotted Apple code that revealed the new colors: black, blue, green, pink, and white.
Otherwise, it is expected to retain the same compact, spherical design as the current model, with no major external changes rumoured. Instead, Apple is reportedly focusing on more powerful internal hardware, with an S9 or newer chip able to support next-generation AI-powered Siri features.
Other changes coming to HomePod mini 2
Alongside a faster processor, the HomePod mini 2 is also rumoured to include:
Apple Intelligence support, enabling the redesigned AI-powered Siri, although some features may arrive after launch if Siri development continues to slip.
Improved connectivity, including Apple’s in-house networking chip, Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip.
Audio improvements, with upgraded drivers and enhanced sound processing.
Minor hardware refinements, such as a removable power cable, although this remains speculative.


						

							


HomePod 3
The larger HomePod is more expensive than the HomePod mini, delivering richer, louder audio with deeper bass and spatial audio. The next generation is expected to get a processor upgrade, improved connectivity and better sound.

				
					

				
			
Michael Brown/Foundry




When is the HomePod 3 expected to launch?
October 2026
Apple has not officially announced a third-generation HomePod, but Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says the company is preparing several new smart home products that are being held back until its redesigned AI-powered Siri is ready. 
If those plans remain on schedule, the HomePod 3 is expected to launch alongside the HomePod mini 2 following the release of the OS 27 updates later this year. 
What changes are coming to the HomePod 3?
Unlike the HomePod mini 2, there are relatively few leaks about hardware upgrades coming to the full-size HomePod. However, it’s expected to receive the same core internal upgrades needed to support Apple’s AI ambitions.
Expected improvements include: 
More powerful chip: The current HomePod uses the S7 chip from the Apple Watch Series 7. A next-generation model is expected to adopt a significantly faster Apple silicon chip, potentially the S9 or newer, to support Apple Intelligence features.
Apple Intelligence Support: The upgraded hardware should enable Apple’s redesigned AI-powered Siri and other Apple Intelligence features, although some capabilities may arrive after launch if Siri development continues to slip.
Improved Connectivity: Rumours point to Apple’s in-house networking chip, together with Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip for improved performance and smart home integration.
Audio Enhancements: Apple is also expected to refine the speaker system with upgraded drivers and audio processing.
In September, a post by itspdfu, who has a history of posting leaks online, said that audioOS27, the operating system for HomePod devices, supports Siri AI. In addition to Siri AI support, the new HomePod will have new animations for the device’s display.
Beyond these internal upgrades, some reports suggest Apple is experimenting with a HomePod featuring a built-in display. That device is expected to be a separate product rather than a standard HomePod 3, and we cover those rumours in the next section.


						

							


HomePod with screen
Apple has been rumored to be working on a HomePod with a screen for years, and while it hasn’t launched yet, the evidence that it’s coming is now overwhelming. Read on to find out what we know about the HomePod with Screen – perhaps called HomePod Touch – based on the latest reports.

				
					

				
			
Foundry and Apple




When will the HomePod with Screen launch? 
Possible launch: Delayed until fall-2026
Apple has been working redesigning the HomePod to include a display for some time. Back in March 2023, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo claimed Apple would “unveil a redesigned HomePod featuring a 7-inch panel.” Kuo initially expected this product to arrive in the first half of 2024, but that timeline slipped. In December 2024, he reported further delays had pushined the launch to after WWDC 2025, citing software development challenges. Then, in March 2025, Kuo suggested the device had been delayed again, due to Apple Intelligence setbacks.
Current speculation suggests a possible release in the fall of 2026, with the release slipping as the major updates to Siri and Apple’s AI platform have been further delayed. Alternatively, the HomePod Touch may gain AI related features as part of a later software update.

				
					

				
			
HomePod with display incoming?

Foundry




What will the HomePod with Screen be like?
Display size: Touchscreen 6 and 7-inches
Software: Custom touchscreen operating system running apps like Weather, Calendar, Photos, HomeKit as well as Apple Music
One of the biggest limitations of today’s HomePod is that almost every interaction relies on Siri. A built-in display would provide a more direct way to control music, manage smart home devices and access information, putting Apple’s device in direct competition with the Amazon Echo Show and Google Nest Hub.
According to current rumours, Apple’s display-equipped HomePod will feature a 6-7-inch touchscreen and run a touch-optimised version of homeOS, allowing it to function as both a smart speaker and a smart home hub. Unlike existing HomePods, it is expected to use a far more powerful A-series chip – possibly an A18 or similar – to support Apple’s redesigned AI-powered Siri and the more demanding graphical interface.
Rumoured features:
Large touchscreen: A 6-7-inch display for controlling smart home devices, viewing photos, checking the weather, following recipes and interacting with apps.
Powerful Apple silicon: An A-series chip is expected to replace the S-series processor used in current HomePods, providing the performance needed for Apple Intelligence and the touchscreen interface.
Dedicated smart home hub: Enhanced HomeKit and Matter controls, with apps including Weather, Calendar, Photos, Apple Music and Home.
Improved connectivity: Apple’s in-house networking chip, Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip are all rumoured.
FaceTime camera: Reports suggest Apple may include a built-in camera for FaceTime and other video-based features.
Possible modular design: Some rumours suggest the display could magnetically dock with a full-size HomePod speaker, allowing it to be used either as a standalone smart display or as part of a higher-fidelity speaker system.
If accurate, this would represent Apple’s biggest expansion of the HomePod lineup since its debut, transforming it from a voice-first speaker into a full smart home controller.

				
					

				
			Amazon Echo Show beside the HomePod mini, 
Ben Patterson/Foundry



							


HomePad or HomeHub smart hub: Rumors & release date for smart display with robot arm
Possible launch: Late 2026 or 2027 if Siri updates are delayed
Strategy: Brand new category of products
HomePad release date 
Apple’s first-ever smart home display had been rumored to launch in the spring of 2026, but it’s been delayed due to issues with Siri, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. He claims the hardware has been ready for some time, according to anonymous sources with knowledge of the matter.
Another leaker, known as Kosutami, who has made accurate predictions in the past, posted on X on March 5 to predict: “Autumn. Home. Integrated with Pad. Now coming.” That somewhat cryptic post doesn’t necessarily refer to the HomePad, but it seems likely. 
What is the HomePad?
Apple has reportedly been exploring a broader smart home strategy for years, and the HomePad could be its most ambitious step yet.
As far back as April 2021, Mark Gurman described a high-end device combining a HomePod speaker, a touchscreen, and a camera mounted on a robotic arm that could follow the user around the room during video calls. Gurman has made various references to this over the years. 
Reports suggest Apple may be planning multiple smart home hub products, potentially split into two tiers:
Low-end smart display (J490): A stationary device with an approximately 7-inch screen, designed for wall mounting or docking. It would focus on HomeKit control and FaceTime calls.
High-end robotic hub (J595): A more advanced version featuring a display mounted on a robotic arm. This “Luxo Jr.-like” device could function as a videoconferencing system and home security tool, though it may not arrive until late 2026 or even 2027.
A revamped, AI-powered Siri is expected to be central to the experience – and its ongoing development is widely believed to be the main reason these products have yet to launch.

				
					

				
			
Imagen 3 (Gemini)




HomePad Smart Hub Design, Features & Specs
Speculation regarding the HomePad’s internal specifications and software capabilities includes:
Processing Power: Internal code suggests the device, codenamed J490, may be powered by the A18 chip, which is capable of supporting advanced Apple Intelligence features.
Operating System: The hub will likely run a version of TVos that incorporates iOS-like features. For instance, the inclusion of the “ChatKit” framework in recent software betas suggests the HomePad may support iMessage and texting, features not currently available on Apple TV or standard HomePods. 
Kitchen Integration: A new “CookingKit” framework and expanded food sections in Apple News indicate that kitchen assistance, such as searching for recipes by ingredient, could be a primary selling point.
Entertainment: Beyond home control, the device is expected to function as an entertainment hub for streaming music and video, as well as making FaceTime calls via a built-in camera.
Advanced Home Control: Code found in the iOS 26 Home app describes an “Adaptive Temperature” feature, which could allow the HomePad to offer more granular control over smart thermostats, including energy-saving optimizations based on local electricity rates.
Camera: There are suggestions that the device could combines a HomePod with a camera, or place a camera on a robot arm. This camera could also be used to recognize gestures. Some years ago a patent was filed that related to a future HomePod that could interpret 3D hand gestures. That patent describes a HomePod that can “interpret three-dimensional hand gestures as a means of controlling the device so as to execute an action or function.”


						

							


What chips will power the new HomePods?
The biggest limitation of today’s HomePods isn’t their speakers – it’s their processors. The HomePod mini still uses the Apple Watch S5 chip introduced in 2019, while the second-generation HomePod runs on the newer, but still relatively modest, S7 chip from the Apple Watch Series 7.
Those chips are powerful enough for music playback, HomeKit control and basic Siri requests, but they are not capable of running Apple’s next-generation AI features. Apple Intelligence currently requires an A17 Pro, M1 or newer chip, making it impossible to bring the full AI-powered Siri experience to the existing HomePod hardware.
That hardware gap is widely believed to be the main reason Apple has delayed its next generation of HomePods. Rather than updating Siri on the existing speakers, Apple is expected to launch new models with significantly faster processors capable of supporting Apple Intelligence.
HomePod mini 2 & HomePod 3
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has said the only confirmed hardware change coming to the new HomePods is a faster chip, although he has not identified which processor Apple will use. The most commonly suggested possibilities are the S9, S10 or S11 chips, but these remain speculative and have not been reported by Gurman or other major Apple analysts.
HomePod with a screen
The display-equipped HomePod is expected to require substantially more processing power than Apple’s existing smart speakers. Because it will reportedly run a touch-based operating system alongside Apple Intelligence, most analysts expect it to use an A-series processor, with an A17 Pro or A18 among the leading predictions. Apple has not confirmed the chip, and these reports remain speculative.
Whatever processors Apple ultimately chooses, the goal appears to be the same across the entire HomePod range: replacing ageing Apple Watch chips with modern Apple silicon capable of delivering the full Apple Intelligence experience.


						

							


New HomePod Prices
The prices for the HomePods increased in June 2026:
HomePod: $349/£349 (was $299/£299)
HomePod mini: $129/£129 (was $99/£99)
With Apple increasing prices in June 2026, we think that these change are like to stick for the updated versions.
However, a HomePod with a built-in screen could command a higher price. It may launch as a separate product altogether, potentially starting around $399/£399, or higher, depending on features.


						

							


Buying advice: Should you wait or buy a HomePod now? 
With prices recently rising on devices that are already underpowered our advice would be: do not buy now. 


						

							


What is on Apple’s Smart Home Roadmap
Apple’s smart-home roadmap is expected to accelerate in 2026 and beyond, as the company expands its Home ecosystem with new hardware, AI features and services designed to compete with Amazon and Google. 
Ongoing: Apple continues to lean on the Matter standard to increase device compatibility. Updates like Matter 1.5 have added support for security cameras and energy management, which Apple is expected to integrate into the Home app.
February 2026: On February 10, 2026, Apple ended support for its legacy HomeKit architecture. This transition removed the ability to use an iPad as a home hub, restricting that role to the Apple TV 4K or HomePod. 
Mid 2026: Launch of new HomePod mini 2 and HomePod 3.
Later in 2026: Apple intends to overhaul Siri. A completely redesigned, LLM-based Siri is expected to debut in early 2026 to power the new smart hubs. Previous delays in the smart home roadmap were largely attributed to Siri’s development “snags”
September 2026: iOS 27 (expected September 2026) may include AI vision recognition, allowing cameras to recognize specific users and their actions to trigger automations while maintaining privacy.
Fall 2026: Launch of Apple’s HomePad device(s).


						

							


Other Smart Home products coming from Apple 
Apple Security Camera: Reports indicate Apple plans to enter the security camera market with its own hardware. Code discovered in iOS 26.2 includes a new “isFirstPartyAccessory” flag, suggesting support for Apple-branded cameras and doorbells that integrate deeply with the ecosystem. 
Robotic HomeHub: A home assistant with a display mounted on a robotic arm

Ron Johnson (left) and Steve Jobs, circa 2001 - image and background shot of Apple Fifth Avenue credit: Apple.

content:
Macworld





		
Apple Mac Studio M5 Max
View Deal
It’s new, it’s uber powerful, and you can get it for $50 off if you buy it from Amazon. What is it? Well, the brand-new Apple Mac Studio with an M5 Max chip, of course. Sure, you could buy it for $2,499 from Apple, but why not get it for $2,449 instead? It’s rare that the Mac Studio is even in stock at Amazon, let alone on sale, so if you want one it’s a great time to buy.
Waiting for a brand-new Apple machine to go on sale usually means waiting a long time. So when a just-launched pro desktop shows up even slightly under list price, it’s worth a look. The Apple Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip is an absolute beast of a device. We actually just reviewed it and found it worthy of our Editors’ Choice award and a 4.5-star rating. We loved the dramatic SSD speed boost and the external display support, even if Apple still won’t let us upgrade the RAM.
The Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip is impressive enough that we think everyone should get one, even if you just got the M4 Max or M3 Ultra. That’s not something we usually say when Apple brings out a new generation of products, but it definitely applies here. It’s easily the best Mac ever made. The M5 Max chip pairs a next-generation CPU with a much more powerful GPU, and it’s built for the kind of heavy lifting that brings lesser computers to a crawl. Video editing, 3D rendering, big creative projects, and complex professional workflows — the Mac Studio won’t even break a sweat.
The memory and storage back it up. This particular configuration comes with 32GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage. Connectivity is generous for such a small device, too, as you get four Thunderbolt 5 ports, as well as plenty of USB-C, USB-A, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. It supports up to five external displays (yes, five!), so you can build out a serious multi-screen setup, and it’s ready for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
For $2,450, this is a professional machine that’s ready for anything you want to accomplish. And you get to buy it for less than what Apple is selling it for, so that’s always a win.
